newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Kredyt Bank eyes Lithuania mkts, privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Kredyt Bank eyes Lithuania mkts, privatisation.

text.p: Poland's Kredyt Bank, which has just received permission to become the first foreign bank to open in Lithuania, said it will be active on financial markets and take part in privatisations in the Baltic state.
The branch is to open in around six months and the share capital is expected to be around five million Ecu.
"We will be active in the inter-bank market and in the Treasury bill market," Kredyt Bank chairman Stanislaw Pacuk told a news conference.
"Probably in the nearest future we will take part in privatisation," he added.
But he said any move of that kind would be carefully considered.
So far Lithuania has been reluctant to sell off its largest and most attractive companies such as the airline and telecommunications company.
But a new right-wing government is about to be installed after the Homeland Union party of independence leader Vytautas Landsbergis won a second round of elections at the weekend.
The Homeland Union has promised to sell the larger companies and attract foreign investors.
"We hope that the new government will further the path of reform," Pacuk said.
Kredyt Bank enters the Lithuanian market as it continues to recover from a banking crisis that hit it at the end of last year, when two of its top banks were closed.
"I think our work here will add to the overcoming of the crisis, even taking into account that we will be competitors," Pacuk added. "Competition can add to positive thinking."
